title: Cadences and harmonic motion
description: Authentic, half, plagal, and deceptive cadences, plus tonic / predominant / dominant jobs.

cards.back: A harmonic (and usually melodic) arrival that creates a sense of pause or close — like punctuation.

cards.front: Name the four common tonal cadence types.
cards.back: Authentic (V→I, often V7→I), half (arrives on V), plagal (IV→I), deceptive (V→vi, not I).

cards.front: What is an authentic cadence and how does it feel?
cards.back: V → I (often V7 → I). Strong arrival at tonic. Perfect/imperfect are subtypes.
The phrase arrives on V. Open; expects continuation.
IV → I. Amen-like close, softer than V–I.
V → vi (not I). Surprise; postpones the tonic.

cards.front: What three jobs does harmonic function group chords into?
cards.back: Tonic (stability), predominant (prepares dominant), dominant (tension toward tonic). Cadences are where those jobs land.

cards.front: Is function a law every genre obeys?
cards.back: No. It is a powerful model for tonal music, not a universal rule.

cards.front: Why do authentic cadences feel conclusive?
cards.back: V (especially V7) contains the leading tone and often the tritone that resolves into tonic chord tones.

cards.front: How do half and deceptive cadences treat dominant energy?
cards.back: A half cadence stops on that tension (on V). Deceptive motion keeps the energy but lands on vi instead of I.

cards.front: What voice-leading moves clarify an authentic close?
cards.back: Leading tone up to tonic, tendency tones resolving, bass motion by fifth.

cards.front: In G major, give one example of each cadence type.
cards.back: Authentic: D | G. Half: G | C | D ending on D. Plagal: C | G. Deceptive: D | Em.

cards.front: In C major, write RN + symbols for each cadence type.
cards.back: Authentic V–I: G (or G7) → C. Half: ends on G. Plagal IV–I: F → C. Deceptive V–vi: G → Am.

cards.front: Voice-lead G or G7 into C, then into Am. Name the cadence types.
cards.back: Into C is authentic (V–I). Into Am is deceptive (V–vi).

cards.front: Why do improvisers care about cadential bars?
cards.back: They are places to resolve — or to deliberately delay resolution. Cadences also mark phrase endings.
